title: Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program Fill Quantities, Days' Supply and Cold-Chain Shipping
content:
A fill on the Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program dispenses the quantity the prescription directs for the days of supply.

## Dispensing rule

**Quantity.** The billing units of a fill are the prescription's billing units per 30 days multiplied by the supply days and divided by 30, rounded up to whole packages, and the supply days of one fill never exceed the tier's maximum days' supply.

**J1817 pump insulin.** J1817 pump insulin is dispensed in billing units of 50 units of insulin, converted from the vials dispensed using the units of insulin per package of each item.

**Cold chain.** Every insulin shipment travels in an insulated shipper with cold packs, validated for the tier's cold-chain validation hours, and ships Monday to Wednesday so that it does not sit in a carrier facility over a weekend.

**Replacements.** A replacement for a temperature excursion or damage never exceeds the units of the shipment it replaces.

## Quantities worked through (hypothetical prescriptions)

| Billing units per 30 days | Supply days | Billing units multiplied by supply days, divided by 30 | Billing units dispensed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 90 | 6 | 6 |
| 3 | 60 | 6 | 6 |
| 2 | 34 | 2.27 | 3 — rounded up to whole packages |
| 1 | 30 | 1 | 1 |

*Hypothetical J1817 conversion:* for a vial holding 1000 units of insulin, the vial corresponds to 1000 divided by 50, that is 20, J1817 billing units.

## Shipping days

| Ship day | Permitted for an insulin shipment? |
|---|---|
| Monday | Yes |
| Tuesday | Yes |
| Wednesday | Yes |
| Thursday, Friday, Saturday or Sunday | No — insulin shipments ship Monday to Wednesday |
